## Hunter Hydrawise support for [Homebridge](https://homebridge.io).
</DIV>
</SPAN>
<!-- MASTHEAD:END -->

`homebridge-hunter-hydrawise` is a [Homebridge](https://homebridge.io) plugin that makes your Hunter Hydrawise irrigation controller available to [Apple's](https://www.apple.com) [HomeKit](https://www.apple.com/ios/home) smart home platform.

### Matter Support

[Matter](https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/) is a cross-ecosystem smart home standard supported by Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Apple Home, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Enabling it here exposes each of your irrigation zones as its own Matter device, **in addition to** the HomeKit accessories this plugin has always provided — HAP is untouched, and everything you have built on it keeps working exactly as before.

This is off by default. Nothing changes until you turn it on.

#### What gets exposed

Each enabled zone becomes its own top-level Matter device. There is no composed parent device and no separate master valve — a flat list of zones is what ecosystems handle most reliably, and it keeps each zone's identity independent of its siblings so renaming or disabling one never disturbs the rest.

By default each zone is exposed as an **on/off outlet**:

  * Turning a zone **on** runs it for its configured run time — the same duration it would have run for on its own schedule.
  * Turning a zone **off** stops it.

State flows the other way too: a zone started from the Hydrawise app, from HomeKit, or by its own schedule shows up in your Matter ecosystem within a polling cycle.

#### Why outlets rather than water valves

Matter defines a `Water Valve` device type, and it is the semantically correct model for an irrigation zone. Unfortunately, as of this writing **Alexa, Google Home, and Apple Home all decline it** — a zone modeled that way simply does not appear in any of them. Amazon's [supported Matter device categories](https://developer.amazon.com/en-US/docs/alexa/smarthome/supported-matter-device-categories.html) omit it entirely.

An on/off outlet is supported everywhere, so that is the default. The cost is that Matter carries no duration with the command, which is why "on" means "run for the zone's configured time". If you need per-run duration control, use HomeKit or MQTT — both still offer it.

If you are commissioning into an ecosystem you have confirmed supports water valves, the `Matter.Valve` feature option switches to the correct device type, including open duration and remaining duration. Changing this rebuilds each zone's Matter device, so they will need to be re-added in your ecosystem.

#### Configuration

There are three steps. The first is Homebridge's, not this plugin's.

**1. Enable Matter on the bridge this plugin runs in.**

Matter is a property of a Homebridge bridge, so it is enabled in your Homebridge configuration rather than in this plugin's settings. Running this plugin in its own **child bridge** is strongly recommended — it keeps this plugin's Matter devices isolated from every other plugin's, so a problem with one cannot affect the rest.

In the Homebridge UI, open this plugin's bridge settings and enable Matter. Or, in `config.json`, add a `matter` block to the plugin's `_bridge`:

```json
{
  "platform": "Hydrawise",
  "_bridge": {
    "username": "0E:11:22:33:44:55",
    "port": 35409,
    "name": "Hunter Hydrawise",
    "matter": {}
  }
}
```

Leave HAP enabled alongside it — that is what keeps HomeKit working. An empty `matter` block lets Homebridge allocate a port; add `"port": 5530` to pin one.

**2. Turn on the `Matter` feature option.**

In the plugin's Settings tab, enable **Matter** at the account, controller, or zone level. It is scoped like every other feature option, so you can expose one controller and not another, or exclude individual zones.

**3. Commission the bridge.**

Once Homebridge restarts you will see the pairing information in the Homebridge log and in the Homebridge UI:

```
[Matter/ChildManager] 📱 Commissioning codes for Hunter Hydrawise:
[Matter/ChildManager]    QR Code: MT:XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
[Matter/ChildManager]    Manual Code: XXXX-XXX-XXXX
```

Add it from your ecosystem's app the way you would add any Matter device. Treat the pairing code like a password — anyone who has it and is on your network can commission your bridge.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not commission this bridge into Apple Home.** Your zones are already in Apple Home over HAP, and commissioning the Matter bridge as well would give you every zone twice.

#### Feature options

| Option | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Matter` | off | account, controller, zone | Expose this controller's zones over Matter, in addition to HomeKit. |
| `Matter.Valve` | off | account, controller | Use Matter's `Water Valve` device type instead of an on/off outlet. See the caveat above — most ecosystems do not support it. |

#### Notes

  * **Matter must be enabled on the bridge.** With the feature option on but Matter not enabled in Homebridge, the plugin logs nothing and behaves exactly as it did before — this is a quiet no-op, not an error.
  * **Restarts are non-disruptive.** Zones are registered from the Matter cache at startup, before this plugin makes its first Hydrawise API call, so your ecosystem does not see them come and go across a restart. A zone's Matter identity is derived from its controller's serial number and its relay id and nothing else, so renaming a zone does not replace the device.
  * **Turning the option off removes the devices.** Zones that are no longer exposed are unregistered rather than merely left un-updated, so they disappear from your ecosystem instead of lingering as unresponsive devices.
  * **Homebridge owns the Matter runtime.** This plugin bundles no Matter library. The Matter server, its storage, port allocation, and commissioning are all Homebridge's, which means Matter behavior tracks your Homebridge version. Homebridge v2.0 or later is required.
